A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe Calibri and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary Sections A-D. Pages 2-13 have identical extracted text and rendered content; page 1 differs only in its arXiv margin stamp.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original model evaluations, ablations, and a human study. Appendices B-D report generation-diversity, reward-model, and optimizer experiments.

after.justification: The same original experiments and human-study results remain in Section 4 and Appendices B-D, including Tables 1-7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3-3.4 retain identical block, layer, and gate scaling, CMA-ES coefficient optimization, and Calibri Ensemble procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same text-to-image tasks, Qwen-generated motivational prompts, T2I-CompBench++ and HPDv3 prompt sets, and human-study coverage. No dataset or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The same FLUX, SD-3.5M, Qwen-Image, and Flow-GRPO comparisons remain in Tables 2-4 and 6. Appendix D retains the same CMA-ES versus Flow-GRPO optimizer comparison.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, training and inference settings, and evaluation procedures are identical. The human study still reports 200 users, 5,600 assessments, and 150 HPDv3 prompts.

E4.justification: Both retain the same block-ablation, scaling-granularity, ensemble-size, and inference-step analyses, plus the diversity, reward-choice, and optimization analyses in Appendices B-D.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 reports five random seeds in both versions, and Table 6 retains identical plus/minus reporting for diversity. No statistical or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match, including Tables 1-7. For example, Table 2 reports FLUX with Calibri at HPSv3 13.48 and 15 function evaluations in both versions.

T1.justification: The architectural equations, calibration optimization formulations, ensemble expression, and CMA-ES mathematical description are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about parameter-efficient calibration, improved generation quality, ensemble benefits, and reduced inference steps.

C2.justification: Interpretations of scaling, diversity preservation, reward generalization, and optimizer convergence are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitation concerning reward models' insufficient sensitivity to visual artifacts.

D1.justification: Calibration hyperparameters in Section 4, parameter and iteration counts and H100 costs in Table 5, and the first-page project link are unchanged.

R1.justification: All 40 references and the related-work discussion are identical, including positioning relative to Stable Flow, FreeFlux, alignment methods, and guidance techniques.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 25 Mar 2026 to v2 dated 29 Jul 2026. Manuscript wording, authors, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page vertical arXiv stamp moves rightward and downward. Figures 1-12, Tables 1-7, captions, and the manuscript's remaining layout are identical.

improvement.justification: The only changes are the first-page arXiv stamp's version, date, and placement. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and substantive presentation remain identical, including the appendices.
